The test image shows tomato leaves with:
- One severely necrotic leaf: large brown areas, dried papery texture, holes where tissue has fallen out
- One yellowing/chlorotic leaf below
- No visible powdery coating, no concentric rings, no velvety mold

Key features: large irregular brown necrotic patches, tissue dropout leaving holes, yellow-green adjacent tissue.

Top candidates: Late_Blight (large brown papery lesions), Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato (scorching/desiccation), Septoria_Leaf_Blotch, Verticillium_Wilt.

Let me view one reference image for Late Blight to confirm.

The Late Blight reference shows a very similar pattern: large irregular brown necrotic areas with remaining green tissue, dry papery texture. This closely matches the test image.

The test image shows advanced Late Blight: large irregular brown necrotic patches that have dried out (tissue dropout leaving holes), with chlorotic yellowing on adjacent leaf tissue. The dry papery texture and large irregular lesion shape are consistent with Late Blight rather than Early Blight (which has concentric rings) or Septoria (which has small circular spots).
